text:
Alex M: quick heads-up — i'm getting pulled into a customer call, need to hand primary off early today. i can be primary until 15:30 PT (about 45m). can someone pick up primary until my normal end at 17:00? there’s a low-sev pager i've been watching for embeddings; it’s flaky but not full outage

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert (pager triggered) — /v1/embeddings error rate > 3% over 5m. Incidence ID: INC-2026-0421. Affected region: us-west-2. Link: https://incident.redwood/internal/INC-2026-0421

oncall-bot: handoff checklist reminder — please: 1) ack any active pager in PagerDuty, 2) set Slack status to "primary oncall", 3) paste any runbook + short summary in thread, 4) update rotation calendar if times change.

Priya Shah: I can take primary until 17:00. acking pager now. Alex — quick ask: what should i look for first? any mitigations you started? :+1:

Alex M: thanks priya. main notes: 1) do NOT restart embeddings workers unless from runbook — restarts can blow cache/KV warming. 2) don't change model variant unless we confirm fallback path; prefer throttling. 3) i've been monitoring errors — mostly 429/503 from a single replica pool. keys:
- runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeds-degrade
- temp mitigation we considered: slow down bulk ingestion clients and enable per-tenant rate-limit at nginx layer (see nginx snippet below)

Sam K: are customers actually seeing errors or is this internal synthetic tests? SLO dashboards show latency spike + small error bump. link: https://console.redwood/metrics/embeds?window=30m

Iris: customer impact: we’re seeing ~5% failed requests for embeddings on a handful of medium tenants; majority get errors as timeouts not 500s. threshold for declaring incident is >10% or >500 failed requests in 15m. right now it's degraded but contained.

Priya Shah: ack — taking this as primary. i'll: 1) ack pager in PD, 2) set Slack status to "primary oncall", 3) open a short overlap call with Alex for 15m in case he needs to hand context (he mentioned a customer call), 4) follow runbook.

Alex M: thanks. quick run commands i used (copy if helpful):
```
# tail recent error traces
rbx logs --service embeddings --env prod --since 10m | jq -r '.entries[] | select(.level=="error") | .message'
# check pool replica health
rbx infra pods --svc embeddings --region us-west-2 | grep Replica
# quick metric snapshot
rbx metrics query --expr 'sum(rate(embeds_requests_errors[5m])) by (replica)'
```

Priya Shah: running those now. i've acked PD and toggled Slack status. also added a short note to the rotation calendar: "Priya primary 15:30-17:00 (midshift swap)". leaving PD note pointing to this thread.

Sam K: if error rate climbs >7% — escalate to L2 @iris and consider routing traffic to fallback model (low-cost embed) per runbook. also watch token-quota throttle alerts, sometimes those correlate.

Iris: noted. fallback steps in runbook: 1) update routing policy to model:embedding-small, 2) enable aggressive KV prefix cache bypass for new requests, 3) notify support to throttle bulk ingestion. preroll the fallback on a single region first (us-west-2) then expand.

Priya Shah: question re PD escalation — do we have the right escalation policy bound to this service? i recall a recent PD change.

oncall-bot: check — service "embeddings-prod" escalation policy: Primary -> Sam K (L1) -> Iris (L2) -> Eng Pager Team. Link: https://pagerduty.redwood/services/embeddings-prod

Priya Shah: ok good. i'll keep an eye and hold until 17:00. i'll also add a tiny overlap meeting (15m) on calendar with Alex for quick debrief after his call. if anything changes i will post a short summary here and update the incident page.

Alex M: perfect. appreciate it. one last nit: if you do enable fallback, please update the incident page with exact traffic percentages and model name — that'll help postmortem.

Priya Shah: will do. taking primary now — acked and monitoring. feel free to DM if you need anything from the call. :phone:

Sam K: thx priya. tagging monitoring alerts i'll watch the dashboards for the next hour.

Iris: thanks team — keeping on-call tidy. i'll stand by for escalation.{{reaction :thumbsup:}}
